verses.1: And after that, Abshalom made a chariot for himself. Then, fifty men rushed forward to go before him.
verses.2: And Abshalom stood on the doorstep. All those who were enemies of him, those who wanted to oppose him in his efforts to go before the king for judgment, called out to him. Abshalom said, “What city is this?” They replied, “We are servants of Israel.”
verses.3: And Abshalom said to him, “See, there are good things about you; you are kind and generous. But I cannot stand against you.”
verses.4: And Abshalom said, “Who will judge me on this earth? Who will stand before me to face all those who are my enemies and whose judgments and just decisions I need to hear?”
verses.5: And it shall be that, when someone approaches to worship him, he shall extend his hand and hold it, and kiss it.
verses.6: And Abshalom did as this was spoken to all the Israelites. They went to the king for judgment, but Abshalom stole the hearts of the people of Israel.
verses.7: And after forty years, Abshalom said to the king, “Let me go and return to my land, which I have dedicated to Jehovah.”
verses.8: For Nedar Nedar, your servant has served you in the wilderness. He said, “If Jehovah allows me to return, I will settle in Jerusalem and serve Jehovah.”
verses.9: And the king said to him, “Go in peace.” So he got up and went away with his companions.
verses.10: And Abshalom sent messengers to all the tribes of Israel, saying, “When you hear the sound of the trumpet, say, ‘Abshalom is king in his own land.’”
verses.11: And they went to Abshalom. Some people from Jerusalem came there, and they went to them. But they didn’t know anything about what was going on.
verses.12: And Abshalom sent Ahithophel the Gileadite to warn David from his city. He offered sacrifices at Giloh. Then the people went and praised Abshalom.
verses.13: And the prophet went to David and said, “There was a man in Israel who was after Abshalom.”
verses.14: And David said to all his servants who were in Jerusalem, “Let us get away from here. There will be no salvation for us from Absalom’s hands. Let us hurry and flee, so that he won’t catch us and destroy us. He will surely destroy the city with fire.”
verses.15: And the servants of the king said to the king, “As for all those whom the king’s officer has chosen, here are your servants.”
verses.16: And the king and all his household went out by foot. The king left behind twelve women to take care of the house.
verses.17: And the king and all the people went out with their feet. They stood at the distance from the house.
verses.18: And all his servants walked before him. And all those who were his slaves, and all those who were under his control… Six thousand men who came from across the land, walking in front of the king.
verses.19: And the king said to me, “My daughter, why do you want to go with us? Return with the king, for you are a foreigner, and you will be taken back to your place.”
verses.20: Today, I will take you with me as we go. I will walk along with you, and I will bring your brothers back with me, in peace and truth.
verses.21: And he said to the king, “May the LORD and my lord, the king, live! For in that place where my lord, the king, will be, whether in death or in life, there you shall have your servants.”
verses.22: And David said to him, “Go ahead, and go through with your journey. I will accompany you, along with all my men and all the soldiers who are with me.”
verses.23: And all the land cries out in great pain. All the people pass by, and the king also passes by along the river Kedron. All the people pass by on the path that leads through the desert.
verses.24: And behold, Zadok and all the Levites also went with him. They carried the ark of God. They carried the Ark of God up to the top of the mountain, so that all the people could see it from outside the city.
verses.25: And the king said to Zedekiah, “Return the Ark of God to the city. If it is pleasing to the LORD, then let me see it and be able to grasp it.”
verses.26: And if he says, “I do not desire you,” then I will do what is good in his eyes.
verses.27: And the king said to Sadok, the high priest: “You shall return to the city in peace. I will appoint Yonatan, son of Abiyatar, as one of your leaders.”
verses.28: See, I am wandering around in the desert until something from your side comes to me and tells me.
verses.29: And Zadok and Abiyatar brought the Ark of God to Jerusalem. They settled there.
verses.30: And David went up to the heights of the mountains. He went there bareheaded. All the people who were with him also went bareheaded as well.
verses.31: And David said, “Ahithophel is with Absalom. Please, LORD, destroy Ahithophel’s plan.”
verses.32: And David came to the mountain where he would worship God. And behold, at his call, the eagle flew up, and its nest was there on the mountain.
verses.33: And David said to him, “If you go ahead of me, then you shall be able to carry me on your shoulders.”
verses.34: And if the city returns, and you say to Abshalom, “You are my king; I will be your servant.” Then from then on, until now, I will be your servant. And you have fulfilled your promise to me.
verses.35: And let Sadoc and the priests listen to what you say there. And whatever you hear from the king’s house, you must tell Sadoc and the priests.
verses.36: There, with them, were their two sons: Ahimeas and Yehonatan. You sent them to me with all the messages they heard.
verses.37: And Husayyah Re’eh of David will come into the city. And Abshalom will also come into Jerusalem.
